The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2025-02-06.45.1) to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a second time. This means they can now consider the bill in greater detail. ### What is the bill's main idea? According to the [bill homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r7277), the bill: > *Amends the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 to separate the Australian Energy Regulator (AER) from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and establish the AER as a non-corporate Commonwealth entity.*
Defence, Veterans’ and Families’ Acute Support Package Bill 2022

The Defence, Veterans' and Families' Acute Support Package Bill 2022 is supported, including the removal of the requirement for warlike service to expand eligibility. The bill aims to improve support for veterans, their families, and children, with the Jamie Larcombe Centre in the Sturt electorate cited as an example of existing services.

The speaker supported the Narcotic Drugs (Licence Charges) Amendment Bill 2022, arguing it simplifies the regulatory framework for medicinal cannabis while maintaining oversight, and noted the industry's potential for domestic medical use, primary production, and export earnings, with proponents in South Australia.
Fair Work Amendment (Paid Family and Domestic Violence Leave) Bill 2022

The speaker supported the Fair Work Amendment (Paid Family and Domestic Violence Leave) Bill 2022, which enshrines in the National Employment Standards the Fair Work Commission’s decision to provide 10 days of paid family and domestic violence leave for all employees, extending the entitlement from the previous five days of unpaid leave for award-covered workers.

The speaker opposed the Jobs and Skills Australia Bill 2022 as a mere cosmetic renaming of the National Skills Commission with no new functions, staff or costs, and criticised the government for excluding restaurants and caterers from the Jobs and Skills Summit while failing to partner with businesses on real skills challenges, particularly in South Australia's defence sector.
Military Rehabilitation and Compensation and Other Legislation Amendment (Incapacity Payments) Bill 2022

The speaker supported the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation and Other Legislation Amendment (Incapacity Payments) Bill 2022, which extends a pilot program for incapacity payments to veterans that lapsed on 30 June, ensuring they are not financially disadvantaged while studying for new careers.
Australian Human Rights Commission Legislation Amendment (Selection and Appointment) Bill 2022

The opposition supported the Australian Human Rights Commission Legislation Amendment (Selection and Appointment) Bill 2022, which introduces statutory merit-based appointment processes, and thanked Sex Discrimination Commissioner Kate Jenkins for her workplace culture report, noting the need for cultural change in Parliament.

The member for Sturt highlighted nearly $200 million in federal-state funded congestion-busting intersection upgrades at Portrush Road-Magill Road ($98 million), Fullarton Road-Cross Road ($61 million), and Fullarton Road-Glen Osmond Road, with the first project now substantially complete. He also noted $7 million for the Kensington Gardens Reserve upgrade, $15 million for the Magill Village Precinct, and a gross pollutant trap on Second Creek.
Electoral Legislation Amendment (Foreign Influences and Offences) Bill 2022

The speaker supported three electoral bills: simplifying authorisation requirements for political materials, expanding telephone voting for voters affected by COVID-19, and closing a loophole to prohibit foreign entities from influencing Australian elections through issue-based campaigns.
